name: Animal Welfare Reading Index
description: An annotated library of writing, research, and data on the welfare of sentient animals.
introduction: Writing, research, and data on what animals experience, how many are affected, and what could change.

categories.title: Sentience and moral consideration
categories.description: What conscious experience is, which animals may have it, and why their experiences matter.

categories.title: Welfare science and measurement
categories.description: How pain, pleasure, health, behavior, and quality of life can be observed and compared.

categories.title: Scale and global data
categories.description: Sources for understanding how many animals are affected and how those estimates are produced.

categories.title: Farmed animals
categories.description: Research and reporting on the lives of animals in food systems and the institutions around them.

categories.title: Aquatic animals and invertebrates
categories.description: Sentience, scale, farming, capture, and welfare for fishes, crustaceans, insects, and other often-neglected animals.

categories.title: Wild animals
categories.description: The welfare of free-living animals, including suffering from natural causes and human activity.

categories.title: Companion and working animals
categories.description: The welfare of animals living and working with people, including shelter and veterinary care.

categories.title: Animals used in research
categories.description: Official records of animal use in science and the severity assigned to experimental procedures.

categories.title: Law and public policy
categories.description: How legal systems classify animals, protect them, and determine which harms are permitted.

categories.title: Ethics in practice
categories.description: Arguments about applying concern for animals to choices, institutions, and social change.

categories.title: Possible futures
categories.description: Proposals for using greater knowledge and technological capacity to reduce suffering more radically.

entries.name: Searching for Animal Sentience
entries.annotation: A systematic review of 2,562 studies published from 1990 to 2012. Nearly all assumed the animals had the emotion or sentience-related trait being studied; only 16 investigated whether it existed. The review also shows how strongly the literature favored vertebrates and negative states such as fear, stress, and pain.
